351.quote_or_event: “False doubts and dream objects - man believes them to be true.”
351.explanation: Bhagat Namdev says that people take illusions and the objects of a dream for real things, which is the root of their bondage.
351.tie_back: The Kural names taking what is not real for the real as the delusion from which lowly birth arises; Namdev names the same error of believing false things to be true.
351.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 485, Raag Aasaa, Bhagat Namdev (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
351._accuracy_note: A strong fit on mistaking the unreal for the real; Namdev does not draw the Kural's explicit link to inglorious rebirth in this line, and the verse is a Bhagat's, not a Guru's.

352.quote_or_event: “The Divine Light shines in their hearts, and like the sun which removes the darkness of night, it dispels the darkness of ignorance.”
352.explanation: Guru Amar Das says that when the Guru's teaching is taken to heart, divine light dawns within and drives out ignorance as the sun drives out night.
352.tie_back: The Kural says that for those freed from delusion, a clear vision drives away the darkness; Guru Amar Das uses the same image of inner light dispelling the dark.
352.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 87, Siree Raag (Sri Raag ki Vaar), Guru Amar Das (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
352._accuracy_note: A strong fit on clear vision dispelling darkness; the Kural's added promise of bliss and freedom from future births is implied in Gurbani but not stated in this line.

353.quote_or_event: “Doubt is dispelled, and the Lord of the Universe is met.”
353.explanation: Bhagat Kabir teaches that when doubt (bharam) is dispelled, God is met.
353.tie_back: The Kural says that for those beyond doubt heaven is nearer than the earth; Kabir likewise puts the meeting with God immediately on the far side of doubt.
353.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 344, Raag Gauree, Bhagat Kabir (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
353._accuracy_note: A strong thematic fit on doubt as the barrier to the divine; Kabir speaks of meeting God rather than of heaven, and the verse is a Bhagat's, not a Guru's.

354.quote_or_event: “You may read and read boat-loads of books; you may read and read and fill pits with them. ... O Nanak, only one thing is of any account: everything else is useless babbling and idle talk in ego.”
354.explanation: In Asa di Vaar Guru Nanak says that any amount of reading and learning is worthless without the one thing that counts, the Lord's Name.
354.tie_back: The Kural says that even complete knowledge gathered through the senses brings no benefit without true knowledge of reality; Guru Nanak dismisses boat-loads of learning in the same way.
354.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 467, Raag Aasaa (Asa di Vaar, salok), Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
354._accuracy_note: A strong fit on outward knowledge being worthless without inner truth; Guru Nanak speaks of book-learning rather than sense-knowledge, and the two lines are quoted with an ellipsis.

355.quote_or_event: “Wherever I look, there I see the Lord pervading.”
355.explanation: Guru Arjan describes the vision of one who has been taught by the Guru: God is seen pervading everything.
355.tie_back: The Kural defines wisdom as seeing the true reality within each thing, whatever it appears to be; Guru Arjan describes seeing the Lord within whatever he looks at.
355.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 193, Raag Gauree, Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
355._accuracy_note: A strong fit on seeing the real within all appearances; Gurbani names that reality as the personal Lord, while the Kural speaks of meypporul, the true thing.

356.quote_or_event: “How rare are those who, as Gurmukh, become Jivan Mukta - liberated while yet alive.”
356.explanation: Guru Amar Das speaks of jivan mukti, liberation while still living, as the rare attainment of the Gurmukh who follows the Guru.
356.tie_back: The Kural says those who have learned and seen the truth here, in this life, set out on the path of no return; Guru Amar Das likewise places liberation within this life.
356.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 232, Raag Gauree, Guru Amar Das (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
356._accuracy_note: A strong fit on liberation in this very life; Sikhism attributes it to the Guru's grace rather than to learning alone.

357.quote_or_event: “True In The Primal Beginning. True Throughout The Ages. True Here And Now. O Nanak, Forever And Ever True.”
357.explanation: The opening salok of Japji Sahib declares that the One is Sat, true and real, in the beginning, through the ages, now and forever.
357.tie_back: The Kural speaks of the mind that has examined and grasped That Which Truly Is; the Japji salok names that Ulladhu, the One who simply is, in every time.
357.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1, Japji Sahib, opening salok, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
357._accuracy_note: Reasonable but partial: both point to Being itself, but the salok is a declaration about God, not a statement that grasping it ends rebirth.

358.quote_or_event: “One whom the Creator Lord unites with Himself, is not consigned to reincarnation.”
358.explanation: In the Patti (acrostic) of Raag Aasaa, Guru Nanak says that whoever the Creator unites with Himself is not born again.
358.tie_back: The Kural says that seeing the perfect Truth removes the folly called birth; Guru Nanak says that union with the Creator likewise ends rebirth.
358.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 433, Raag Aasaa (Patti), Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
358._accuracy_note: Reasonable but partial: both end rebirth, but Gurbani does not call birth a folly and attributes release to the Creator's uniting grace rather than to seeing truth.

359.quote_or_event: “Meditate on the One, O my mind, who is the Support of all.”
359.explanation: Guru Arjan tells the mind to meditate on the One God, the support of all beings.
359.tie_back: The Kural says that whoever understands the true Support of all things will be free of the sorrows that cling; Guru Arjan names that Support and asks the mind to rest on it.
359.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 51, Siree Raag, Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
359._accuracy_note: Reasonable but partial: it shares the idea of one true Support, but this line does not mention the falling away of lesser attachments or of the sorrows they bring.

360.quote_or_event: “I have brought the ten sensory organs under my control, and erased every trace of the five thieves.”
360.explanation: Bhagat Namdev says he has mastered the senses and wiped out the five thieves (kaam, krodh, lobh, moh, ahankar); the Gurmukhi says even their name (naavau) is erased.
360.tie_back: The Kural says that when desire, anger and delusion are destroyed so completely that even their names are gone, suffering ends; Namdev claims to have erased the very name of the passions.
360.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 693, Raag Dhanaasree, Bhagat Namdev (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
360._accuracy_note: Near one-to-one, including the image of erasing even the name; Gurbani's list is five thieves rather than the Kural's three, and the verse is a Bhagat's, not a Guru's.
